messages:
mike-cust: Hey team — after our scheduled cert rotation last night we started seeing intermittent TLS failures from our app to the private endpoint. Go client errors: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority. ~1-2% of requests fail. Not a full outage but affects users. Rotation finished 2026-03-16T22:03:xxZ. Please advise.
claire: Thanks — can you share the exact client error and how you're calling the endpoint (curl, sdk, Go)? Also any quick repro steps you can run?
mike-cust: Error from pod logs: 
```
2026-03-17T00:12:45Z http: TLS handshake error from 10.2.1.14:54321: remote error: tls: unknown certificate
error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
We call https://vpc.example.internal via Go net/http. I ran a quick openssl against the hostname and got mixed results depending on which IP I hit.
jordan: Can you run `openssl s_client -connect vpc.example.internal:443 -servername vpc.example.internal -showcerts -status` and paste the output? Also try resolving the hostname (may be multiple backend IPs). Possible causes: a backend still serving an old/incomplete chain, or DNS caching sending you to a stale instance.
mike-cust: Here's condensed `openssl -showcerts` results hitting two IPs (A and B):
```
# IP A
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-private
   i:/CN=intermediate-ca
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
# IP B
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-private
   i:/CN=intermediate-ca
 1 s:/CN=intermediate-ca
   i:/CN=root-ca
verify return:1
```
So IP A returns an incomplete bundle (missing intermediate cert).
tom: On our side the rotator reported success on both nodes but node-2 logged: `rotate: write bundle failed: file exists` around the time of the job. That could explain an atomic-write bug where bundle ended up truncated or not replaced, leaving the old bundle missing the intermediate. I'm looking at the rotator logs now.
deploy-bot: rotate-cert-job/private-proxy completed for node-1 at 1789004600, node-2 at 1789004623 (exit code 0) :white_check_mark:
jordan: Logs show node-2 had a non-fatal error during the file replace workflow; service didn't reload after the partial write. So node-2 kept serving the previous (incomplete) bundle. That matches the openssl evidence.
claire: Also worth double-checking: if your VPC blocks egress to OCSP/CRL endpoints, some clients will treat stapled responses differently. Do you have any egress allowlists that could affect OCSP queries or stapling? Time skew can also cause intermittent verification failures.
mike-cust: Our default egress policy blocks unknown hosts, but we had allowed the common public OCSP endpoints; internal CA OCSP wasn't whitelisted. System clock is in sync (NTP, <5s skew). I can open the internal OCSP host to test.
jordan: Two quick repro steps for support playbook: 1) `nslookup vpc.example.internal` to list IPs; 2) `curl --resolve vpc.example.internal:443:<IP>` to target a single backend and see if errors reproduce; 3) `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername vpc.example.internal -showcerts -status` to inspect the chain and stapling. If curl fails against one IP but not the other, it's almost certainly a per-node bundle issue.
mike-cust: Confirmed — `curl --resolve vpc.example.internal:443:10.10.2.8 https://vpc.example.internal/health` fails with the x509 error, while hitting 10.10.2.9 succeeds. I'll keep a capture if you want.
tom: I'll force a reload on node-2 now and then re-run the rotator with the atomic-write fix queued. Reloading node-2 at 1789005200.
jordan: After reload, `openssl` from your env should show the full chain on both IPs. We're also going to add a verification step in the rotator to check the served chain via local s_client before marking the host complete.
mike-cust: Reload confirmed fixed on my side — errors dropped to 0% after hitting the reloaded IP. Thanks for the quick triage. Please keep me posted about the rotator fix so we can avoid future drifts.
claire: We'll follow up with a short postmortem and patch for the rotator (atomic write + verify + reload). For your side, if you keep OCSP egress locked down, please whitelist your internal CA OCSP endpoints to avoid validation edge cases. Thanks :thumbsup:
mike-cust: Thanks everyone — appreciate the help, closing for now unless we see recurrence.
